name: World Health Organization (WHO)
summary: The World Health Organization is the United Nations' specialized agency for international public health, headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland. It sets global health norms and standards, coordinates responses to international disease outbreaks, and provides technical support to national health systems, particularly in lower-income countries. It is funded through a mix of mandatory member-state assessments and voluntary contributions, the latter of which make up the large majority of its budget and give major donors significant informal influence over its priorities.
history: Founded in 1948 as part of the post-World War II push to build permanent international institutions, WHO's constitution formally took effect on April 7, 1948 — still marked annually as World Health Day. Its early flagship achievement was the global smallpox eradication campaign, declared successful in 1980, the only human disease eradicated through deliberate intervention to date. It later led global responses to HIV/AIDS, established the International Health Regulations framework governing how countries report outbreaks, and played a central, closely scrutinized role during the COVID-19 pandemic beginning in 2020, including its much-debated early timeline for declaring a Public Health Emergency of International Concern.
impact: WHO's clearest historical impact is smallpox eradication, which by most estimates has prevented hundreds of millions of deaths in the decades since. It maintains the International Classification of Diseases (ICD), used by virtually every national health system for diagnostic coding and mortality statistics, and its Essential Medicines List influences drug procurement policy worldwide. It is also a genuinely contested institution: criticized from different directions for being too slow and diplomatically cautious in emergencies (raised repeatedly around COVID-19), for being overly dependent on a small number of large voluntary donors, and for the practical limits of an organization with no enforcement power over sovereign member states.
